label: cluster encryption level
type: the level of encryption imposed on inter-node communication, settable only after node-to-node encryption is enabled: `control` (the default when enabling), `all`, or `strict` - where `strict` additionally forbids unencrypted client connections. Loopback traffic within a single node stays exempt even under `strict`.
aliases_note: Two spellings for one setting, licensed by the procedure page that uses both wordings for the same control: "Establish an appropriate encryption-level for the cluster" alongside the `clusterEncryptionLevel` REST/CLI parameter it is set with. Filed under the tier-neutral kebab name in the tls: subject area rather than under the parameter spelling. 2 + 2 files, zero overlap.
evidence: The cluster encryption-level can only be configured after cluster encryption itself has been _enabled_.
The `--enable` flag enables node-to-node encryption for the cluster, at the default level of `control`.
`strict`, meaning `all` with only encrypted communication permitted between nodes and between the cluster and external clients.
If node-to-node encryption needs to be disabled, ensure that the `clusterEncryptionLevel` for the cluster is set to `control` first.
note: The disable path is the interesting half and appears only in the procedures: you cannot simply turn node-to-node encryption off, you must first step the level back down to `control`. That is an ordering constraint on a teardown, the category of fact a reference page has no reason to carry, and round 26 found it stated on two different node-management pages and on neither security reference page.
